hints: A definition of velocity needs both the changing quantity and a time interval.
Use displacement rather than distance: velocity is change in displacement divided by time.
walkthrough: Velocity describes how displacement changes with time.
State the definition as change in displacement divided by time, or rate of change of displacement.

ai_rubric.observable: Defines velocity as change in displacement per unit time, or as the rate of change of displacement.

hints: The resistive forces are negligible, so the stated driving force is the resultant force on the car.
Rearrange F = ma to a = F / m, using 2400 N and 1200 kg.
walkthrough: Because resistive forces are negligible, the resultant horizontal force is 2400 N.
Apply F = ma: a = F / m = 2400 / 1200 = 2.0 m s⁻².

ai_rubric.observable: Applies F = ma to 2400 N and 1200 kg and obtains 2.0 m s⁻².

hints: The car starts from rest and the driving force is constant while resistance is negligible, so its acceleration remains constant.
Use the 2.0 m s⁻² acceleration from part (b)(i) to locate the velocity at 20 s, then draw the corresponding velocity–time line.
walkthrough: The car starts from rest, so the velocity–time graph starts at the origin.
A constant acceleration produces a straight-line velocity–time graph with a constant positive gradient.
Using v = u + at, the velocity at 20 s is 0 + (2.0 × 20) = 40 m s⁻¹.
Draw and label line A as a straight line from (0, 0) to (20 s, 40 m s⁻¹).

ai_rubric.observable: Draws and labels A as a straight line from the origin with positive gradient.
Makes line A end at 20 s and 40 m s⁻¹.

hints: At the start the car is at rest, so air resistance is zero and the initial acceleration matches line A.
As speed increases, air resistance reduces the resultant force and hence the gradient of the velocity–time graph; at 12 s the forces balance.
walkthrough: Line B starts at the origin with the same initial gradient as A because air resistance is initially zero.
As the car speeds up, air resistance rises, reducing the resultant forward force and making the gradient steadily decrease; B remains below A.
At 12 s, air resistance equals the driving force, so the resultant force and acceleration are zero.
From 12 s to 20 s, draw B as a horizontal line at the terminal velocity and label it B.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws B from the origin with the same initial gradient as A and keeps it below A thereafter.
Shows B with a decreasing gradient until it reaches zero.
Draws B horizontally from 12 s to 20 s and labels the line B.

hints: Immediately after the driving force rises, compare the new driving force with the air resistance at the old terminal speed.
The temporary resultant force accelerates the car; as speed rises, air resistance rises until the forces balance again.
walkthrough: At 20 s the car is travelling at its old terminal speed, where the air resistance previously balanced 2400 N.
Increasing the driving force to 3000 N makes the forward force greater than the air resistance, so the car accelerates and its velocity increases.
As the velocity increases, air resistance increases until it balances 3000 N.
The car then travels at a new, higher terminal velocity.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the velocity increases, or equivalently that the car accelerates after the driving force rises.
States that the car reaches a new, higher terminal or constant velocity.
